CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields (_contract, _provenance, _internal, _guard) NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. D6′ LOCKED: utilization-stack economics lead frame; anchor-plus-fill removed as lead. Upside rows are never summed into base totals.

fn1.text: Pricing and experience rates are benchmarked to Boston operators' published 2025–26 fares.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships. Seat estimates assume 3.0% capture of on-site headcount, a planning estimate.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect posted harbor speed limits. Speed-rule relief appears only as a separately labeled upside, never in base cases. Precedent: an electric hydrofoil exemption on Stockholm's Route 89.

fn5.text: Fleet counts are planning figures, not a timetable. A working fleet plan typically adds ~10–15% spare capacity, not yet included here.

fn6.text: Crew costs are benchmarked to published Boston-area wage data with a buffer for wage growth to 2026; shift structure to be confirmed in an operations walkthrough.

fn7.text: Spot-seat volumes are backed into each scenario's monthly total from the stated fill rate (10–30%) and fare band ($45–$65/leg); not separately itemized in the source model. Figures rounded to the nearest seat-leg.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in ~15% of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day. Commuter bundles are the schedule spine; experiences, charters, spot seats and overnight lines buy down payback.

revenue_rows.note: A discounted monthly pass — 3–4× an MBTA monthly, ~50–60% below a door-to-door ride-hail substitute.
Yield-managed seats on spare commute capacity and shoulder sailings; fill assumed thin at 10–30%.

opex_rows.note: Electric operation across commute, midday, evening and weekend sailings.
Range spans smaller-vessel service history up to a $100K/yr ceiling for the N45.
Two crew (captain + deckhand) at $85/hr combined, loaded, across a full service day.

opex_labels_v1.energy: Canon 4.1 kWh/nm @ $0.30/kWh × stacked daily activity (commute legs + midday/evening/weekend sailings). Electric-operation assumption.
opex_labels_v1.maintenance: N45 NOT validated — N30 canon ($65K/yr) floor, $100K/yr stated ceiling assumption, ÷12.
opex_labels_v1.crew: Benchmark-validated 2026-08-15 — 2-crew (captain + deckhand), $85/hr combined loaded, extended to stacked hours. Basis: BLS OEWS Boston metro means (May 2023) x 1.4294 ECEC burden = $77.16/hr; $85 = ~3%/yr wage drift to 2026 (assumption, labeled). Shift structure (split shifts for 16-hr stacked day) to ops walkthrough.
opex_labels_v1.insurance: Placeholder, weak basis — hull/liability ~1.5–3%/yr of insured value + illustrative berth fee loosely anchored to one documented commercial rate; not a Navier-specific quote.

layer_pricing_basis_v1.committed_bundles_L1: $950–1,275/seat-month — priced as a discounted pass vs premium spot (industry pass discounts 26–51%: MBTA ~26%, Seastreak 40-trip ~35%, NYC Ferry ~36%, Blade ~44–51%); 3–4× MBTA monthly ($319); ~50–60% below door-to-door substitute (Uber Salem→Boston ~$56/trip ≈ $2,460/mo). Status v1: Benchmark-anchored; canon-consistent; no Boston operations yet.
layer_pricing_basis_v1.spot_seats_L2: $40–65/leg, yield-managed — bounded by Seastreak $30 and Uber door-to-door ~$55–56; matches approved corridor fare (Boston↔Hingham $65). Status v1: Benchmark-anchored; fill rates unproven, modeled thin (10–30%).
layer_pricing_basis_v1.experiences_charters_L3: Experiences $59–79/pp (Boston market: BHCC sunset $49 → Odyssey dinner $77–98, whale watch $75); charters $550–600/hr (Boston Charter Boat $550/hr, 25-pax, 2-hr min). Status v1: Market-priced (Boston operators cited); not yet operated by Navier; conservative case ≈ ⅓ of one incumbent daily sailing.
layer_pricing_basis_v1.sponsorship_U1: $150K/yr fleet-level placeholder — precedents: Citi Bike ~$7–8M/yr system, Santander Cycles £6.25M/yr, Cleveland HealthLine line-naming $250K/yr, Barclays station $200K/yr. Status v1: Precedent-priced; no marine-transit precedent; never per-vessel headline.
layer_pricing_basis_v1.overnight_cargo_U2: ~$350/run contract, 16 nights/mo — anchored to published waterborne tariffs (Casco Bay Lines 2026: $0.108–0.162/kg generic freight ⇒ $216–324 per ~2,000 kg run) + medical-courier premiums (Dropoff 2026: $30–100/job, refrigerated $3.50–5.25/mi). Status v1: Published-tariff-anchored; not yet operated by Navier; harbor cargo earns courier-linehaul rates, NOT island air-substitute rates ($0.75–1.50/kg canon does not apply where roads exist). First cargo classes: medical/lab specimens, batch parcels, catering/event — clean, high-value, night-moving. Seafood REJECTED as first class (odor/leakage/sanitation in premium cabin; commodity-priced $2.50–3.75/box).

_provenance.stack_frame_v1: One asset, one day, four demand layers. A commuter-only vessel monetizes ~15% of available hours; the stack monetizes the day. Commute is the strategic backbone and schedule spine; experiences, charters, spot and overnight lines buy down payback.
_provenance.payback_summary_v1: conservative ~21 yr (cash-positive, not financeable); mid ~4.3 yr — headline; upside ~2.1 yr (incl. sponsorship + cargo upside lines). Indicative ranges only, conservative default. Upside comes from utilization layers with cited market prices and from more corridors activating — never from inflating per-layer assumptions.
_provenance.speed_relief_row_v1: With authority speed-rule relief (precedent: Stockholm Candela P-12 exemption). Not quantified for Boston this pass — renders as a labeled upside row without numbers. Never blended into base or mid cases; base economics respect posted limits.
_provenance.scenarios_label_v1: Per-vessel N45 ($2.5M capex), no anchor subsidy in any case. Ranges + assumptions, conservative default. Every unproven layer enters base case only at deliberately thin utilization.
_provenance.upside_scenario_detail_v1: Includes sponsorship ($3.1K/mo per vessel, fleet-level ÷4) + overnight cargo ($5.6K/mo). Converges with canon partner-corridor payback (Boston↔Hingham 2.49 yr) — same physics: all-day premium utilization.
_provenance.scenario_qa_v1: Mid case is the financeable headline — requires L3 execution at roughly half the sailing cadence of Boston's incumbent experience operators, at prices below their dinner tier. Conservative shown always. Upside labeled. Crew rate benchmark-validated vs BLS Boston (loaded mean $77.16/hr May 2023; model uses $85 with wage-drift buffer); shift structure pending ops walkthrough.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil, not a boat with a battery.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the chop for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional boats. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.
